title: Head, Health Economics
description: Vantive is a vital organ therapy company on a mission to extend lives and expand possibilities for patients and care teams everywhere. For 70 years, our team has driven meaningful innovations in kidney care. As we build on our legacy, we are deepening our commitment to elevating the dialysis experience through digital solutions and advanced services, while looking beyond kidney care and investing in transforming vital organ therapies. Greater flexibility and efficiency in therapy administration for care teams, and longer, fuller lives for patients— that is what Vantive aspires to deliver. We believe Vantive will not only build our leadership in the kidney care space, it will also offer meaningful work to those who join us. At Vantive, you will become part of a community of people who are focused, courageous and don’t settle for the mediocre. Each of us is driven to help improve patients’ lives worldwide. Join us in advancing our mission to extend lives and expand possibilities. The Head of HE, China is a senior leadership role accountable for shaping and leading the Health Economics strategy for China. This role will provide strategic thought leadership on health system trends, policy evolution, reimbursement dynamics and economic evidence needs, translating external insights into actionable access strategies that support patient access and strengthen the value proposition for Vantive’s chronic and acute portfolios. As the functional leader for Health Economics, the role is responsible for setting direction, prioritizing resources, supervising the development and dissemination of pharmacoeconomic strategies and tools, and ensuring strong alignment with Medical, Market Access, Government Affairs, Commercial and global teams so that clinical and access strategies are grounded in robust economic evidence and adapted to China market needs. The role will act as a strategic partner and influencer to senior business leaders, enabling the commercial force, marketing teams, health professionals and administrative stakeholders to understand therapy value, economic impact and access implications. The Head of HE will also build organizational capability by translating complex health economics concepts into clear, practical insights for decision making. The Head of HE must demonstrate strong leadership in navigating the access process for new health technologies in China, proactively identifying clinical, administrative, policy and economic barriers, and leading cross-functional actions to address them in support of sustainable access and business priorities. Key Responsibilities: Lead strategic discussions with business unit, product, access, government affairs and medical leaders to define HE priorities, evidence plans, studies and therapy economic tools aligned with portfolio and access objectives. Provide leadership and subject matter expertise in Health Technology Assessment, reimbursement policy, real-world evidence and health economic evaluation to guide strategic decision making. Oversee the design and development of high-quality HE models, value tools and evidence-generation initiatives based on representative clinical and pharmacoeconomic studies, local data needs and identified evidence gaps. Ensure economic evaluations, evidence outputs and stakeholder materials meet high standards of quality, integrity, compliance and timely delivery. Champion the use of credible official sources, local evidence and external insights to generate compelling analyses, presentations and value narratives for internal and external stakeholders. Partner with global teams as the China HE voice to ensure global strategies reflect local market nuances and, where required, lead local evidence generation to address China-specific access and payer requirements. Provide leadership support for Government Affairs and Market Access engagement by shaping evidence-based narratives, preparing for key stakeholder discussions and ensuring follow-up actions are connected to broader strategic objectives. Build and lead the HE function with clear priorities, strong governance, effective cross-functional collaboration and a culture of accountability, strategic thinking and continuous capability development.
